A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantial reorganization, both PDFs describe the same mirror-descent preference-optimization work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hopper and Three-Legged Ant experiments in Tables 1–3, plus Gemma fine-tuning and AlpacaEval results in Section 4.3.

after.justification: v2 reports original MuJoCo experiments in Table 2 and Appendix H, and Gemma fine-tuning results in Table 3.

M1.justification: v1 learns the functions ψ and ϕ⁻¹ with a fixed logarithmic transformation. v2 additionally learns a monotone transformation g in the MPO objectives and introduces LPO and CoLPO, including probability-dependent constraints and clipping. The training-progress-dependent variant presented in v1 is no longer included.

E1.justification: Hopper, Three-Legged Ant, and Gemma-7B alignment remain the core tasks. However, v1's LLM dataset replaces half the responses with Gemma-2B outputs, whereas v2 uses dpo-mix-7k with its naturally mixed quality. Hopper coverage also narrows from several generating-agent skill levels to expert/bad-agent datasets.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons expand substantially beyond v1's primarily ORPO-based tables. v2 Table 2 includes RRHF, SLiC-HF, DPO, IPO, CPO, ORPO, R-DPO, SimPO, SFT, and LPO. Appendix H compares five existing methods on Hopper, and the LLM comparison adds CPO and SLiC-HF alongside ORPO.

E3.justification: v1 uses shared MuJoCo hyperparameters tuned for ORPO; v2 reports searches for each algorithm–dataset combination and specifies 10 SFT epochs followed by 2 preference-optimization epochs for two-step baselines. LLM evaluation changes from test accuracy and a direct comparison against ORPO to evaluation against GPT-4 using Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as judge, with length-controlled win rates.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-versus-learned-g and one-step-versus-two-step comparisons, a matrix testing discovered objectives across dataset conditions, higher-noise TLA evaluations, and LLM chosen/rejected probability diagnostics. v1's temporal-awareness ablations disappear, and its numerical judge-temperature analysis is replaced by a brief qualitative discussion.

E5.justification: TLA retains means and standard errors over 25 agents. v2 newly reports standard errors for LLM win rates and length-controlled win rates, and describes confidence-interval overlap when highlighting TLA results. Conversely, the Hopper table no longer explicitly identifies its run count or the meaning of its ± values.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, reported ORPO base-TLA performance changes from 3277±49 to 3087±322 under the revised tuning protocol. v1's 57%/62% LLM accuracies and 53% direct-comparison win rate disappear; v2 instead reports CoLPO win rate/length-controlled win rate of 31.94%/24.01%, versus ORPO's 24.47%/19.25%. These different experimental conditions do not establish a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: v2 generalizes the formal reward-estimation criterion from log-sigmoid to g composed with sigmoid, with g increasing, and correspondingly broadens the MPO objectives. Theorem 3.1, its KKT proof, and the mirror-map/Bregman-divergence derivations are otherwise retained, moving from Appendices A–B to C–D.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from analyzing ORPO failures and directly transferring discovered losses to establishing a broader diagnostic benchmark and designing CoLPO from MuJoCo-derived insights. Claims now address a much larger baseline set. Temporal awareness is no longer a stated contribution.

C2.justification: v1 explains improvements mainly through smaller, noise-mitigating and temporally adjusted updates. v2 emphasizes continued optimization after chosen trajectories become more likely than rejected ones, interprets SFT's differing effects on noisy and mixed-quality data, and motivates CoLPO's constraint against improving relative preference by reducing both probabilities.

D1.justification: v2 adds simplified formulas with coefficients for discovered losses in Appendix H and documents fitness estimation using 100 trajectories per perturbed agent. Its LLM reporting expands from a reference to Alignment Handbook defaults to explicit LoRA, batching, learning-rate, sequence-length, epoch, and objective settings in Section 5 and Appendix J. These are substantial added disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands discussion and citations covering preference-learning origins, additional PO algorithms, evolution strategies, and meta-learning alternatives, particularly in Appendices A and E–G. The original positioning relative to DiscoPOP and f-DPO largely survives in Appendix B rather than being removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Hopper and related work move into appendices, LLM transfer becomes a standalone section, and new background subsections reorganize the explanation around MPO and the broader comparisons.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two. v2 adds an algorithm-objective summary table, restructures TLA results into a large comparison matrix, and adds LLM result and hyperparameter tables. The earlier gradient and temporal-progress figures are replaced by a consolidated comparison of SimPO, ORPO, and two discovered objectives.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens comparative validation beyond v1's mostly ORPO-based evidence through tuned baselines, component comparisons, and cross-setting evaluations. Length-controlled LLM results, uncertainty reporting, and explicit implementation settings also improve assessability. Hopper coverage narrows, and Appendix H.3 incorrectly singles out SimPO despite IPO reaching 1606±91 in Table 4, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and transparency.
